## Introduction

For our project, we are interested in exploring how instant noodle ratings differ across countries and brands.
Since the dataset contains reviews from different places, I want to take a closer look at how people rate instant noodles and whether some patterns can be found across countries.

In this EDA, I will mainly focus on the relationship between country and rating, the distribution of ratings, and how the number of reviews may relate to the ratings.
Rather than assuming that the highest-rated noodles are necessarily the best, I want to first understand what the data actually shows and what limitations might affect our comparisons.

## Data Source and Description

The dataset used in this analysis comes from The Ramen Rater, a website that reviews instant noodle products from different countries.
I obtained the dataset from the TidyTuesday project, which published the data on June 4, 2019.

The dataset contains 3,180 reviews and six variables, including brand, variety, packaging style, country, and star rating.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

ramen <- read_csv("../data/raw/ramen_ratings.csv")

```

```{r}
glimpse(ramen)
```

```{r}
summary(ramen)
```

Finding: The median rating (3.75) is slightly higher than the mean rating (3.688)

## Investigate missing values and zero ratings

Before cleaning, I want to know exactly which records are missing ratings and whether the zero ratings are actual observations.

```{r}
# Check missing values
colSums(is.na(ramen))

ramen |>
  filter(is.na(stars))

ramen |>
  filter(stars == 0)

problems(ramen)
```
```{r}
library(visdat)

vis_dat(ramen)
```

::: callout-tip
## Initial Data Observations

The initial inspection shows that the dataset contains 3,180 reviews and six variables.
Most variables are complete, but there are some missing values in `review_number`, `style`, and `stars`.

The average rating is 3.688, while the median is 3.75.
The middle 50% of ratings fall between 3.25 and 4.50.
This suggests that ratings are generally concentrated toward the higher end of the scale, although the distribution needs further investigation.

Before conducting comparisons, I will investigate the missing ratings and check whether zero ratings represent valid reviews.
:::

## Data Cleaning

```{r}
ramen_rated <- ramen |>
  filter(!is.na(stars))

dim(ramen_rated)
```

```{r}
colSums(is.na(ramen_rated))
```

::: callout-note
**Data Cleaning Decisions**

I decided to keep the 33 zero-rated products because The Ramen Rater uses a rating scale from 0 to 5, where zero represents the lowest possible rating rather than a missing value.

However, I removed the 14 reviews with missing star ratings from the rating analysis because they cannot be included when calculating average ratings.
I kept the original dataset unchanged and created a separate dataset for the analysis.
:::

## Research Questions

**1.How do instant noodle ratings vary across countries? Which countries have the highest average ratings, and how many products from each country have been reviewed?**

**2.How do ratings differ across brands and packaging styles? Do certain brands or packaging types tend to receive higher ratings?**

**3.Do spicy instant noodles tend to receive higher ratings than non-spicy varieties? Does this pattern vary across countries?**

```{r}
country_summary <- ramen_rated |>
  group_by(country) |>
  summarise(
    average_rating = mean(stars),
    total_reviews = n()
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(average_rating))

country_summary
```

# Rating Distribution by Country
```{r}
# ratings by country
country_plot_data <- ramen_rated |>
  group_by(country) |>
  summarise(
    average_rating = mean(stars),
    total_reviews = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(total_reviews >= 10) |>
  arrange(average_rating)

ggplot(country_plot_data,
       aes(x = average_rating,
           y = reorder(country, average_rating),
           size = total_reviews)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, color = "blue") +
  labs(
    title = "Average Instant Noodle Ratings by Country",
    x = "Average rating",
    y = "Country",
    size = "Number of reviews"
  ) +
  xlim(0, 5)
```

```{r, fig.width=15, fig.height=18}
# Rating Distribution by Country
ggplot(
  ramen_rated,
  aes(
    x = stars,
    y = reorder(country, stars, FUN = median)
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    fill = "white",
    color = "black",
    width = 0.65,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Instant Noodle Ratings Across Countries",
    x = "Star Rating",
    y = "Country"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme_gray()
```

# Rating Distribution_Reviers
How are instant noodle ratings distributed across all reviews?
```{r}
ggplot(ramen_rated, aes(x = factor(stars))) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Instant Noodle Ratings",
    x = "Star Rating",
    y = "Number of Reviews"
  ) +
  theme_gray() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  country_summary |> filter(total_reviews >= 10),
  aes(
    x = average_rating,
    y = reorder(country, average_rating),
    color = average_rating,
    size = total_reviews
  )
) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "skyblue", high = "tomato") +
  labs(
    title = "Average Ratings by Country",
    x = "Average Rating",
    y = "Country",
    color = "Average Rating",
    size = "Number of Reviews"
  ) +
  theme_gray()
```

## Research Question 2
How do ratings differ across brands and packaging styles? Do certain brands or packaging types tend to receive higher ratings?



```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}

brand_summary <- ramen_rated |>
  group_by(brand) |>
  summarise(
    average_rating = mean(stars),
    total_reviews = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  slice_max(total_reviews, n = 15) |>
  mutate(brand = reorder(brand, average_rating))

ggplot(brand_summary,
       aes(x = average_rating, y = brand)) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = 0, xend = average_rating,
        yend = brand),
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = total_reviews),
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_color_gradient(
    low = "skyblue",
    high = "red"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 5),
    breaks = 0:5
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Ratings by Brand",
    x = "Average Rating",
    y = "Brand",
    color = "Number of Reviews"
  ) +
  theme_gray(base_size = 13)
```

## Research Question 3
Do spicy instant noodles tend to receive higher ratings than non-spicy varieties? Does this pattern vary across countries?

```{r}
ramen_spicy <- ramen_rated |>
  mutate(
    spice_type = if_else(
      str_detect(str_to_lower(variety), "spicy"),
      "Spicy",
      "Non-spicy"
    )
  )
```


```{r}
spicy_comparison <- ramen_spicy |>
  group_by(country, spice_type) |>
  summarise(
    average_rating = mean(stars),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(n >= 5) |>
  group_by(country) |>
  filter(n_distinct(spice_type) == 2) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
ggplot(spicy_comparison,
       aes(x = spice_type,
           y = average_rating,
           group = country,
           color = country)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Spicy vs. Non-spicy Ratings Across Countries",
    x = "Noodle Type",
    y = "Average Rating",
    color = "Country"
  ) +
  theme_gray()
```
